title: Platform Nine
logline: A man waits every night for a midnight train that never stops, until the morning shows who is really waiting for whom.
look: Realistic night station in rain, sodium lamps and wet reflections, handheld documentary camera that lags behind the action; a hard cut to flat grey daylight and an overgrown, abandoned platform.
narrator: female, elderly, moderate pitch, british accent
An elderly widow, steady and loving, with a catch in the voice
music: Rain, distant rail hum, a station clock tick; trains roar past with wind; a single piano phrase in daylight; a train finally hissing to a stop.

shots.direction: WS 35mm handheld · slow drift · fade in — night platform, sodium lamps, rain; a man on a bench beside a suitcase
CU 85mm handheld · cut — the station clock at 11:58; the second hand ticks but never moves on
WS 24mm handheld shake · cut — a train roars through without stopping; light streaks, wind
MS 50mm handheld · cut — the man stands, watches it go, sits back down
WS 24mm · cut — another train, faster, does not stop
CU 85mm handheld · cut — his hands hold a wet ticket
WS 35mm · lamp flicker · cut — for a few frames the platform is overgrown and broken, then normal again
MS 50mm handheld · slow push · cut — he looks up at the clock: still 11:58
WS 35mm locked · hard cut to day — flat grey daylight: the platform abandoned, overgrown, the bench empty
MS 50mm handheld · cut — an old woman with flowers walks slowly to the bench
CU 85mm · hold · cut — she lays the flowers by a small plaque on the bench and sits where he sat
WS 35mm · locked · fade out — a train arrives and, for the first time, stops; doors open; she stays seated and smiles

narration.text: He said he'd meet my train at midnight.
Some people wait for a long time.
I come every year, so he has someone to wait for.
narration.tone: warm, a catch in the voice

narration.text: One day I'll take the train. Not yet.
